question: Which state of India is known as 'Land of Rolling Hills'?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Mizoram__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Mizoram

__
 
• Mizoram is known as the "Land of rolling mountains" because it has a huge number of mountains.
 
• It is also known as the "Molasses Basin". The state is made up of soft, unconsolidated deposits.
 
• Mizoram's mountainous geography contains many foreland basins, which are valley-type depressions that run parallel to mountains.
 
• When unconsolidated deposits fill up these depressions, it is called the Molasses Basin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Tripura

__
 
• It is a state in northeast India.
 
• It's bordered by Bangladesh, Mizoram, and Assam, and is a hilly region with a surface area of 10,486 square kilometres.

Nagaland

 
• It is a state in northeast India, bordering Myanmar.
 
• It's a mountainous state with a land area of 16,579 square kilometres.
 
• Nagaland is one of India's smaller states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__

Molasses basin

 
• The Molasses basin is a foreland basin, to the north of the Alps.
 
• It is formed during the Oligocene and Miocene epochs.
 
• The basin formed as a result of the flexure of the European plate under the weight of the Orogenic wedge of the Alps that was forming to the south.
 
• In geology, the name "Molasses basin" is also used in a general sense for a synorogenic (formed contemporaneously with the orogen) foreland basin of the type north of the Alps.
